_comment: Permissions policy for the fde-sor Lambda execution role. This role holds the keys to two things that are not ours: a customer's system-of-record credentials and the per-engagement actor-hash salts. Note what is absent -- there are NO Postgres permissions here, because database authorization is enforced at the SQL layer (SET LOCAL ROLE fde_ingest, see fde_mcp.db). This policy only gets the function to a place where it CAN open a connection; db/010 and db/014 decide what that connection may do. Replace ${AWS_REGION} and ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} at deploy time. The SQS resource is scoped to a naming convention; narrow it to the exact queue ARNs once the adapters are registered.

Statement._comment: Three distinct secrets under one prefix: the database login (fde/db/*), the per-customer SoR credential named by sor.adapter.secret_arn (fde/sor/*), and the per-engagement actor-hash salt (fde/actor-hash-salt/*). GetSecretValue only -- nothing here rotates or writes a secret.
The event-source mapping polls on the function's behalf using these permissions. DeleteMessage is what the EKS long-poll consumer uses after a batch commits; the Lambda path never calls it itself.
Backfill reads a customer's historical export. Read-only: a backfill that could write to the export bucket could rewrite the evidence it is about to ingest.
One topic, for critical control_bypass escalation from the drift scan (docs/08 section 7).

Required for VpcConfig: Lambda creates and deletes an ENI in the database's subnets on the function's behalf. These actions do not support resource-level permissions, which is why the Resource is * -- the ec2:Subnet condition narrows it to the subnets you actually deploy into.
